newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures still down late on forecasts.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures still down late on forecasts.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained lower late Tuesday in sluggish trade, undermined by forecasts for milder weather next week despite some support this week from the season's first cold snap, sources said.
At 1350 EST, December was still down by 6.8 cents at $2.665 per million British thermal units, while January was 6.4 cents lower at $2.675. Most others were down by 1.5 to 2.6 cents.

"We failed to get through resistance, and with the weather looking more moderate next week, we could see a little more downside," said one Houston-based trader, adding recent volatility had scared some to the sidelines.
While the technicals looked somewhat bearish today after December's failure to break resistance in the $2.75 area, traders noted trendline support at $2.59-60 was still intact.
With conflicting signals and little clear direction, most agreed volume would remain relatively light near-term.
But fundamental traders expected milder weather next week to soon pressure the physical market.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices firmed slightly Tuesday to the low-$2.70s. Midwest prices firmed a few cents to the mid-$2.60s. Cold weather drove New York city gate swing gas up 10-15 cents to the low-to-mid $3.40s. December gas in New York was quoted at $1.25 over the screen, or in the $3.90s.
NYMEX said 25,867 contracts traded at 1320 EST.
NYMEX Alberta natgas was still untraded at 1345 EST but December remained bid 1.5 cents higher at $1.315.
NYMEX Permian natgas also was untraded at 1345 EST.
On the KCBT, December remained seven cents lower at $2.465, while deferreds were still down by 3.5 to 7.5 cents. The December East/West spread widened by 0.2 cent to 20.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
